        - AWS
            - Cloud computing concept
                - 1. What Is Cloud Computing?
                    
                    Cloud computing means:
                    
                    > Using computing resources (servers, storage, databases, networking, software, AI, etc.) over the internet instead of owning and managing physical hardware yourself.
                    > 
                    
                    Instead of buying servers:
                    
                    - You rent them
                    - Use them when needed
                    - Pay only for usage
                    - Scale instantly
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Traditional Infrastructure (Before Cloud)
                    
                    Imagine you build a startup.
                    
                    You need:
                    
                    - Servers
                    - Cooling systems
                    - Electricity
                    - Networking equipment
                    - Security
                    - Backup systems
                    - Database machines
                    - Physical datacenter space
                    
                    This is called:
                    
                    # 🏢 On-Premise Infrastructure
                    
                    Problems:
                    
                    | Problem | Explanation |
                    | --- | --- |
                    | Expensive | Need huge upfront cost |
                    | Slow scaling | Buying servers takes weeks/months |
                    | Maintenance | Hardware failures, upgrades |
                    | Overprovisioning | Buy too much “just in case” |
                    | Underprovisioning | Traffic spike crashes app |
                    | Global deployment hard | Need datacenters worldwide |
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Cloud Computing Solves This
                    
                    Cloud providers like:
                    
                    - Amazon Web Services
                    - Microsoft Azure
                    - Google Cloud Platform
                    
                    already own massive datacenters.
                    
                    You rent resources from them instantly.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Real Analogy
                    
                    ## ❌ Traditional Way
                    
                    Buying a power generator for your house.
                    
                    You:
                    
                    - maintain it
                    - repair it
                    - fuel it
                    - replace it
                    
                    ## ✅ Cloud Way
                    
                    Using electricity from the grid.
                    
                    You:
                    
                    - just consume
                    - pay for usage
                    - provider handles infrastructure
                    
                    Cloud computing is basically:
                    
                    # “Electricity model for computing”
                    
                - [2. How](http://2.How) cloud computing works
                    
                    Cloud providers have:
                    
                    - millions of servers
                    - worldwide datacenters
                    - virtualization systems
                    - networking systems
                    - orchestration software
                    
                    You request resources through:
                    
                    - dashboard
                    - API
                    - CLI
                    - Infrastructure as Code
                    
                    Provider allocates virtual resources instantly.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Example Flow
                    
                    You deploy Node.js backend.
                    
                    Without cloud:
                    
                    - Buy machine
                    - Install Linux
                    - Configure networking
                    - Maintain everything
                    
                    With AWS:
                    
                    - Create EC2 instance in 1 minute
                    - Deploy app
                    - Done
                    
                    AWS handles:
                    
                    - hardware
                    - datacenter
                    - networking backbone
                    - power
                    - availability
                - 3.Core Technologies Behind Cloud
                    
                    # A. Virtualization
                    
                    One physical server can run multiple virtual servers.
                    
                    Example:
                    
                    Physical server:
                    
                    - 256 GB RAM
                    - 64 CPU cores
                    
                    Can be split into:
                    
                    - VM1 → 8GB
                    - VM2 → 16GB
                    - VM3 → 32GB
                    
                    etc.
                    
                    This enables:
                    
                    - isolation
                    - efficient usage
                    - multi-tenancy
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # B. Hypervisor
                    
                    Software managing virtual machines.
                    
                    Examples:
                    
                    - VMware
                    - KVM
                    - Xen
                    
                    AWS originally heavily used Xen.
                    
                    Hypervisor:
                    
                    - allocates CPU
                    - RAM
                    - storage
                    - networking
                    
                    to VMs.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # C. Distributed Systems
                    
                    Cloud is not one server.
                    
                    It is:
                    
                    - thousands of servers
                    - spread globally
                    - connected together
                    
                    This gives:
                    
                    - high availability
                    - redundancy
                    - fault tolerance
                    - scaling
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # D. Automation & APIs
                    
                    Everything in cloud is programmable.
                    
                    Example:
                    
                    ```
                    aws ec2 run-instances
                    ```
                    
                    AWS creates server automatically.
                    
                    This is why DevOps exists.
                    
                - 4.Important Characteristics of Cloud Computing
                    
                    According to NIST cloud model:
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # A. On-Demand Self-Service
                    
                    You provision resources yourself instantly.
                    
                    Example:
                    
                    - create server in 30 seconds
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # B. Broad Network Access
                    
                    Accessible from anywhere via internet.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # C. Resource Pooling
                    
                    Provider shares infrastructure among customers securely.
                    
                    Called:
                    
                    # Multi-Tenancy
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # D. Rapid Elasticity
                    
                    Scale up/down instantly.
                    
                    Example:
                    
                    - Black Friday traffic spike
                    - auto scale from 2 → 100 servers
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # E. Measured Service
                    
                    Pay-as-you-go billing.
                    
                    Like utilities:
                    
                    - electricity
                    - water
                - 5. Types of Cloud Deployment
                    
                    # A. Public Cloud
                    
                    Owned by provider.
                    
                    Examples:
                    
                    - AWS
                    - Azure
                    - GCP
                    
                    Most common.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # B. Private Cloud
                    
                    Dedicated cloud for one organization.
                    
                    Example:
                    
                    - Bank internal cloud
                    
                    More control/security.
                    
                    More expensive.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # C. Hybrid Cloud
                    
                    Combination:
                    
                    - some workloads on-prem
                    - some in cloud
                    
                    Very common in enterprises.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # D. Multi-Cloud
                    
                    Using multiple cloud providers.
                    
                    Example:
                    
                    - AWS + Azure
                    
                    Reasons:
                    
                    - avoid vendor lock-in
                    - redundancy
                    - special services
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # 5. Cloud Service Models (MOST IMPORTANT)
                    
                    This is where:
                    
                    - IaaS
                    - PaaS
                    - SaaS
                    
                    come from.
                    
                - 6. Cloud Service Models (MOST IMPORTANT)
                    
                    # 5. Cloud Service Models (MOST IMPORTANT)
                    
                    This is where:
                    
                    - IaaS
                    - PaaS
                    - SaaS
                    
                    come from.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Understanding the Responsibility Model
                    
                    Question:
                    
                    # “Who manages what?”
                    
                    Different models give different responsibility levels.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # A. IaaS — Infrastructure as a Service
                    
                    You rent infrastructure.
                    
                    Provider manages:
                    
                    - hardware
                    - networking
                    - virtualization
                    
                    You manage:
                    
                    - OS
                    - runtime
                    - application
                    - database
                    - security configs
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Example AWS Services
                    
                    - Amazon EC2
                    - Amazon EBS
                    - Amazon VPC
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Real Example
                    
                    You create Ubuntu EC2.
                    
                    You must:
                    
                    - install Node.js
                    - configure Nginx
                    - patch OS
                    - secure server
                    - deploy app
                    
                    AWS only gives VM.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Think Of It Like
                    
                    # Renting an empty apartment
                    
                    You furnish/manage everything inside.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # B. PaaS — Platform as a Service
                    
                    Provider manages:
                    
                    - infrastructure
                    - OS
                    - runtime
                    - scaling
                    
                    You only deploy code.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Example Services
                    
                    - AWS Elastic Beanstalk
                    - Heroku
                    - Google App Engine
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Real Example
                    
                    Upload Node.js app.
                    
                    Platform:
                    
                    - provisions servers
                    - handles scaling
                    - installs runtime
                    - load balancing
                    - monitoring
                    
                    You focus only on:
                    
                    - business logic
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Think Of It Like
                    
                    # Renting fully furnished apartment
                    
                    You just live inside.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # C. SaaS — Software as a Service
                    
                    Complete software delivered over internet.
                    
                    Provider manages EVERYTHING.
                    
                    You only use software.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Examples
                    
                    - Google Workspace
                    - Notion
                    - Slack
                    - Zoom
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Think Of It Like
                    
                    # Staying in hotel
                    
                    Everything managed for you.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Responsibility Comparison
                    
                    | Layer | On-Prem | IaaS | PaaS | SaaS |
                    | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
                    | Networking | You | Provider | Provider | Provider |
                    | Storage | You | Provider | Provider | Provider |
                    | Servers | You | Provider | Provider | Provider |
                    | Virtualization | You | Provider | Provider | Provider |
                    | OS | You | You | Provider | Provider |
                    | Runtime | You | You | Provider | Provider |
                    | Application | You | You | You | Provider |
                    | Data | You | You | You | Some shared |
                - 7. AWS Specifically
                    
                    Amazon Web Services launched in 2006.
                    
                    It provides:
                    
                    - compute
                    - storage
                    - databases
                    - networking
                    - AI
                    - serverless
                    - analytics
                    - security
                    - DevOps tools
                    
                    AWS is mostly:
                    
                    # IaaS + PaaS
                    
                    while also offering SaaS products.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # AWS Global Infrastructure
                    
                    AWS consists of:
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # A. Regions
                    
                    Physical geographic areas.
                    
                    Examples:
                    
                    - us-east-1
                    - eu-central-1
                    - ap-south-1
                    
                    Each region is isolated.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # B. Availability Zones (AZ)
                    
                    Each region contains multiple datacenters.
                    
                    Example:
                    
                    - us-east-1a
                    - us-east-1b
                    
                    Purpose:
                    
                    - fault tolerance
                    
                    If one AZ fails:
                    
                    - another survives
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # C. Edge Locations
                    
                    Used for CDN:
                    
                    - caching
                    - low latency
                    
                    Service:
                    
                    - Amazon CloudFront
                - 8. Why Companies Love Cloud
                    
                    # Speed
                    
                    Deploy globally in minutes.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Scalability
                    
                    Auto-scale during traffic spikes.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Reliability
                    
                    Redundant systems.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Cost Efficiency
                    
                    No upfront hardware purchase.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Global Reach
                    
                    Deploy near users worldwide.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Managed Services
                    
                    Focus on business instead of infrastructure.
                    
                - 9. Modern Cloud Concepts
                    
                    # A. Serverless
                    
                    You do not manage servers.
                    
                    Example:
                    
                    - AWS Lambda
                    
                    Upload function only.
                    
                    AWS handles:
                    
                    - scaling
                    - runtime
                    - servers
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # B. Containers
                    
                    Package app with dependencies.
                    
                    Example:
                    
                    - Docker
                    
                    AWS services:
                    
                    - ECS
                    - EKS
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # C. Infrastructure as Code (IaC)
                    
                    Infrastructure written as code.
                    
                    Tools:
                    
                    - Terraform
                    - CloudFormation
                    
                    Example:
                    
                    ```
                    Create EC2
                    Create DB
                    Create Load Balancer
                    ```
                    
                    automatically.
                    
                - 10. Shared Responsibility Model (VERY IMPORTANT)
                    
                    AWS secures:
                    
                    - cloud infrastructure
                    
                    You secure:
                    
                    - applications
                    - IAM permissions
                    - data
                    - OS configs (for EC2)
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Example
                    
                    If your EC2 hacked because:
                    
                    - weak password
                    - open SSH
                    - vulnerable Node.js app
                    
                    That is YOUR responsibility.
                    
                    Not AWS.
                    
                - 11. Most Important Mental Model
                    
                    Cloud is NOT magic.
                    
                    It is:
                    
                    # “Someone else’s datacenter + automation + APIs + virtualization”
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Real Example Mapping
                    
                    Your current experience already touches cloud concepts:
                    
                    | What You Did | Cloud Concept |
                    | --- | --- |
                    | EC2 deployment | IaaS |
                    | Nginx reverse proxy | Networking |
                    | Docker Compose | Containerization |
                    | PM2 process manager | App runtime management |
                    | DigitalOcean droplet | Cloud VM |
                    | Cloudflare | CDN/edge network |
                    | Auto backups | Cloud storage/automation |
                    | PostgreSQL on EC2 | Self-managed DB |
                    | Vercel | PaaS |
            - IAM-AWS Identity and Access Management
                - 1. What Is IAM?
                    
                    IAM =
                    
                    # Identity + Authentication + Authorization
                    
                    It controls:
                    
                    - WHO can access AWS
                    - WHAT they can access
                    - WHAT actions they can perform
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Real World Analogy
                    
                    Imagine a company office.
                    
                    You have:
                    
                    - employees
                    - managers
                    - admins
                    - security guards
                    
                    Not everyone should:
                    
                    - enter every room
                    - access financial systems
                    - delete company data
                    
                    IAM is basically:
                    
                    # AWS security and permission system
                    
                - 2. Core IAM Components
                    
                    
                    | Concept | Purpose |
                    | --- | --- |
                    | Users | Individual identities |
                    | Groups | Collection of users |
                    | Roles | Temporary assumable identities |
                    | Policies | Permission rules |
                    | Permissions | Allowed/denied actions |
                - 3. IAM Users
                    
                    An IAM User represents:
                    
                    # One identity/person/application
                    
                    Example:
                    
                    - Developer
                    - DevOps engineer
                    - Backend service
                    - CI/CD pipeline
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # User Has:
                    
                    - username
                    - password (optional)
                    - access keys (optional)
                    - attached policies
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Example
                    
                    ```
                    Muzaffar
                    ```
                    
                    This IAM user may have:
                    
                    ```
                    Allow:
                    - EC2 read
                    - S3 upload
                    
                    Deny:
                    - IAM delete
                    - Billing access
                    ```
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Authentication vs Authorization
                    
                    VERY IMPORTANT.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Authentication
                    
                    # “Who are you?”
                    
                    AWS checks:
                    
                    - password
                    - access key
                    - MFA
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Authorization
                    
                    # “What are you allowed to do?”
                    
                    AWS checks:
                    
                    - IAM policies
                - 4. IAM Policies (MOST IMPORTANT PART)
                    
                    Policies define permissions.
                    
                    They are JSON documents.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Example Policy
                    
                    ```
                    {
                      "Version":"2012-10-17",
                      "Statement": [
                        {
                          "Effect":"Allow",
                          "Action":"s3:PutObject",
                          "Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket/*"
                        }
                      ]
                    }
                    ```
                    
                    This means:
                    
                    ```
                    ALLOW upload objects into my-bucket
                    ```
                    
                - 5.Policy structure deep dive
                    
                    # 5. Policy Structure Deep Dive
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # A. Effect
                    
                    ```
                    "Effect":"Allow"
                    ```
                    
                    or
                    
                    ```
                    "Effect":"Deny"
                    ```
                    
                    AWS supports:
                    
                    - explicit allow
                    - explicit deny
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # IMPORTANT RULE
                    
                    # Explicit Deny ALWAYS wins
                    
                    Even if another policy says Allow.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # B. Action
                    
                    Defines API actions.
                    
                    Examples:
                    
                    ```
                    "Action":"ec2:StartInstances"
                    ```
                    
                    ```
                    "Action":"s3:GetObject"
                    ```
                    
                    ```
                    "Action":"*"
                    ```
                    
                    means ALL actions.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # C. Resource
                    
                    Defines WHAT resources.
                    
                    Example:
                    
                    ```
                    "Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket/*"
                    ```
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # D. Condition
                    
                    Optional extra restrictions.
                    
                    Example:
                    
                    ```
                    "Condition": {
                      "IpAddress": {
                        "aws:SourceIp":"192.168.1.0/24"
                      }
                    }
                    ```
                    
                    Meaning:
                    
                    - only allow from certain IPs
                - 6. What Is ARN?
                    
                    ARN =
                    
                    # Amazon Resource Name
                    
                    Unique identifier for AWS resources.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Example
                    
                    ```
                    arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket
                    ```
                    
                    Structure:
                    
                    ```
                    arn:partition:service:region:account-id:resource
                    ```
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Example
                    
                    ```
                    arn:aws:ec2:us-east-1:123456789012:instance/i-123456
                    ```
                    
                - 7. How AWS Permission Evaluation Works
                    
                    THIS IS CRITICAL.
                    
                    When request comes:
                    
                    ```
                    Can user start EC2?
                    ```
                    
                    AWS evaluates:
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Step 1 — Authenticate
                    
                    Who is making request?
                    
                    - IAM user?
                    - IAM role?
                    - service?
                    - federated identity?
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Step 2 — Gather Policies
                    
                    AWS collects:
                    
                    - attached user policies
                    - group policies
                    - role policies
                    - resource policies
                    - SCPs (organizations)
                    - permission boundaries
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Step 3 — Evaluate
                    
                    AWS checks:
                    
                    ```
                    Is action explicitly denied?
                    ```
                    
                    If YES:
                    
                    ❌ denied immediately
                    
                    Else:
                    
                    ```
                    Is action explicitly allowed?
                    ```
                    
                    If YES:
                    
                    ✅ allowed
                    
                    Else:
                    
                    ❌ denied by default
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # VERY IMPORTANT
                    
                    AWS is:
                    
                    # Default Deny System
                    
                    If not explicitly allowed:
                    
                    - denied automatically
                - 8. IAM Groups
                    
                    Groups simplify permission management.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Example
                    
                    Group:
                    
                    ```
                    Developers
                    ```
                    
                    Policy:
                    
                    ```
                    Allow EC2 and CloudWatch access
                    ```
                    
                    All users in group inherit permissions.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Instead of:
                    
                    Adding same permissions to 100 users.
                    
                    You:
                    
                    - create group
                    - attach policy once
                - 9. IAM Roles (VERY IMPORTANT)
                    
                    Roles confuse many engineers initially.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Core Idea
                    
                    A role is:
                    
                    # A temporary assumable identity with permissions
                    
                    Unlike users:
                    
                    - roles usually have NO permanent credentials
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Real Analogy
                    
                    Imagine hotel room access card.
                    
                    You temporarily receive:
                    
                    - access permissions
                    - limited duration
                    
                    After expiration:
                    
                    - access gone
                - 10. Why Roles Exist
                    
                    Roles solve HUGE security problems.
                    
                    Without roles:
                    
                    - applications need hardcoded AWS credentials
                    
                    VERY dangerous.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Example BAD Practice
                    
                    ```
                    constaccessKey="AKIA...."
                    constsecret="abcd..."
                    ```
                    
                    If leaked:
                    
                    - AWS compromised
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Roles fix this.
                    
                - 11. How IAM Roles Work
                    
                    Suppose:
                    
                    - EC2 server needs S3 access
                    
                    Instead of:
                    
                    - storing access keys
                    
                    You:
                    
                    1. Create IAM role
                    2. Attach permissions
                    3. Attach role to EC2
                    
                    AWS automatically gives temporary credentials.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Flow
                    
                    ```
                    EC2 Instance
                       ↓
                    Requests temporary credentials
                       ↓
                    AWS STS generates temporary credentials
                       ↓
                    EC2 uses them automatically
                    ```
                    
                - 12. What Is STS?
                    
                    Service:
                    
                    AWS Security Token Service
                    
                    Generates:
                    
                    - temporary access keys
                    - session tokens
                    
                    Used heavily in:
                    
                    - IAM roles
                    - federation
                    - cross-account access
                - 13. Temporary Credentials
                    
                    Temporary credentials include:
                    
                    - Access Key ID
                    - Secret Access Key
                    - Session Token
                    - Expiration time
                    
                    Much safer.
                    
                - 14. Role Trust Policy
                    
                    # A. Permission Policy
                    
                    What role CAN do.
                    
                    Example:
                    
                    - read S3
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # B. Trust Policy
                    
                    Who CAN ASSUME the role.
                    
                    Example:
                    
                    ```
                    {
                      "Effect":"Allow",
                      "Principal": {
                        "Service":"ec2.amazonaws.com"
                      },
                      "Action":"sts:AssumeRole"
                    }
                    ```
                    
                    Meaning:
                    
                    - EC2 service may assume role
                - 15. Role Assumption
                    
                    AssumeRole means:
                    
                    # “Temporarily become this role”
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Example
                    
                    Developer account:
                    
                    - limited permissions
                    
                    Temporarily assume:
                    
                    ```
                    ProductionAdminRole
                    ```
                    
                    for:
                    
                    - deployment
                    - maintenance
                    
                    After session expires:
                    
                    - access removed
                - 16. Common IAM Role Use Cases
                    
                    # A. EC2 → S3
                    
                    Very common.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # B. Lambda → DynamoDB
                    
                    Lambda assumes role automatically.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # C. Cross-Account Access
                    
                    One AWS account accesses another.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # D. GitHub Actions Deployment
                    
                    CI/CD assumes deployment role.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # E. Kubernetes IRSA
                    
                    Pods assume AWS roles.
                    
                - 17. Managed Policies vs Inline Policies
                    
                    # Managed Policy
                    
                    Reusable.
                    
                    Can attach to many users/roles.
                    
                    Example:
                    
                    - AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess
                    
                    AWS provides many built-in policies.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Inline Policy
                    
                    Directly embedded into:
                    
                    - one user
                    - one role
                    
                    Not reusable.
                    
                - 18. Principle of Least Privilege
                    
                    MOST IMPORTANT SECURITY PRINCIPLE.
                    
                    Give ONLY required permissions.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # BAD
                    
                    ```
                    "Action":"*",
                    "Resource":"*"
                    ```
                    
                    Admin everywhere.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # GOOD
                    
                    ```
                    "Action":"s3:GetObject",
                    "Resource":"specific-bucket"
                    ```
                    
                    Minimal permissions.
                    
                - 19. IAM Permission Boundaries
                    
                    Advanced concept.
                    
                    Permission boundary =
                    
                    # maximum allowed permissions
                    
                    Even if role policy allows more:
                    
                    - boundary restricts it
                    
                    Useful in enterprises.
                    
                - 20. Resource-Based Policies
                    
                    Not all permissions are identity-based.
                    
                    Some resources have their own policies.
                    
                    Example:
                    
                    - S3 bucket policies
                    - Lambda resource policies
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Example
                    
                    S3 bucket itself may allow:
                    
                    ```
                    Account B can read this bucket
                    ```
                    
                - 21. IAM Evaluation Logic (Advanced)
                    
                    AWS evaluates:
                    
                    1. Authentication
                    2. SCPs
                    3. Resource policies
                    4. Identity policies
                    5. Permission boundaries
                    6. Session policies
                    
                    Final result:
                    
                    - allow
                    - deny
                - 22. MFA (Multi-Factor Authentication)
                    
                    VERY important.
                    
                    Extra security layer.
                    
                    Requires:
                    
                    - password
                    - OTP/app/device
                    
                    Especially critical for:
                    
                    - root account
                    - admins
                - **23. Root Account vs IAM User**
                    
                    # Root Account
                    
                    Created with AWS account.
                    
                    Has FULL unrestricted access.
                    
                    Should:
                    
                    - rarely be used
                    - enable MFA
                    - avoid daily operations
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # IAM Users
                    
                    Used for actual operations.
                    
                - 24. Real Backend Example
                    
                    # BAD Architecture
                    
                    ```
                    Hardcoded AWS keys in .env
                    ```
                    
                    Problems:
                    
                    - leaks
                    - rotation difficult
                    - security risk
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # GOOD Architecture
                    
                    ```
                    EC2 instance
                       ↓
                    Attached IAM role
                       ↓
                    Temporary credentials
                       ↓
                    S3 access
                    ```
                    
                    No hardcoded secrets.
                    
                - 25. How SDK Uses Roles Automatically
                    
                    AWS SDK checks credential chain.
                    
                    Example order:
                    
                    1. Environment variables
                    2. Shared config
                    3. IAM role metadata endpoint
                    
                    For EC2:
                    
                    ```
                    http://169.254.169.254/
                    ```
                    
                    metadata service provides temporary credentials.
                    
                - 26. Most Important IAM Concepts For Interviews
                    
                    
                    | Concept | Importance |
                    | --- | --- |
                    | Users vs Roles | VERY HIGH |
                    | Policies | VERY HIGH |
                    | Explicit deny | VERY HIGH |
                    | Least privilege | VERY HIGH |
                    | STS | HIGH |
                    | AssumeRole | HIGH |
                    | Resource policies | HIGH |
                    | Temporary credentials | HIGH |
                    | Cross-account roles | HIGH |
                    | MFA | HIGH |
                - 27. Mental Model To Remember Forever
                    
                    # IAM User
                    
                    Permanent identity.
                    
                    Example:
                    
                    ```
                    Human developer
                    ```
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # IAM Role
                    
                    Temporary identity.
                    
                    Example:
                    
                    ```
                    EC2 temporarily accessing S3
                    ```
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # Policy
                    
                    Permission rules.
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # STS
                    
                    Temporary credential generator.
                    
                - FINAL
                    
                    # AWS IAM In One Sentence
                    
                    # “IAM decides WHO can do WHAT on WHICH resource under WHICH conditions.”

            - 1.Overall
                
                # Amazon S3 — Overall
                
                ## What is Amazon S3?
                
                Amazon Web Services [Amazon S3](https://aws.amazon.com/s3/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) (**Simple Storage Service**) is a cloud-based **object storage service** used to store, retrieve, manage, and process data at massive scale.
                
                S3 stores data as:
                
                - objects
                    
                    inside
                    
                - buckets
                
                ---
                
                # Simple Meaning
                
                S3 is basically:
                
                ```
                Internet-scale cloud storage
                ```
                
                where applications can store:
                
                - images
                - videos
                - backups
                - logs
                - documents
                - datasets
                - archives
                - static websites
                - AI/ML data
                
                ---
                
                # Why Amazon S3 Exists
                
                Traditional storage systems have problems:
                
                - limited scalability
                - hardware maintenance
                - disk failures
                - expensive infrastructure
                - backup complexity
                - difficult replication
                - global access problems
                
                S3 solves these by providing:
                
                ```
                Highly scalable, highly durable, globally accessible storage
                ```
                
                without managing physical servers/disks manually.
                
                ---
                
                # What Type of Storage is S3?
                
                S3 is:
                
                ```
                Object Storage
                ```
                
                NOT:
                
                - block storage
                - traditional filesystem
                
                ---
                
                # What is Object Storage?
                
                In object storage:
                
                - every file becomes an object
                - object contains:
                    - file data
                    - metadata
                    - unique key
                
                ---
                
                # S3 Core Structure
                
                ```
                Bucket
                 ├── Object
                 ├── Object
                 └── Object
                ```
                
                Example:
                
                ```
                my-backups/
                 ├── january.zip
                 ├── february.zip
                 └── march.zip
                ```
                
                ---
                
                # Main Components of S3
                
                | Component | Meaning |
                | --- | --- |
                | Bucket | Container for objects |
                | Object | Stored file/data |
                | Key | Unique object path/name |
                | Metadata | Information about object |
                | Storage Class | Defines storage behavior |
                | Versioning | Multiple object versions |
                | Bucket Policy | Access control |
                | Lifecycle Rule | Automatic object management |
                
                ---
                
                # Where S3 Is Used
                
                S3 is used almost everywhere in cloud systems.
                
                ---
                
                # Common Use Cases
                
                | Use Case | Example |
                | --- | --- |
                | File uploads | User profile pictures |
                | Backups | PostgreSQL dumps |
                | Static websites | React frontend |
                | CDN origins | CloudFront |
                | Logs | Application logs |
                | Data lakes | Analytics systems |
                | AI/ML | Training datasets |
                | Media storage | Videos/images |
                | Archives | Long-term compliance |
                
                ---
                
                # Real Backend Example
                
                Your backend:
                
                ```
                Frontend
                 ↓
                Backend API
                 ↓
                Generate presigned URL
                 ↓
                Frontend uploads directly to S3
                 ↓
                S3 stores file
                 ↓
                RDS stores object metadata
                ```
                
                ---
                
                # Important S3 Characteristics
                
                | Feature | Meaning |
                | --- | --- |
                | Massive scalability | Virtually unlimited storage |
                | High durability | 11 nines durability |
                | High availability | Highly accessible |
                | Multi-region support | Global infrastructure |
                | Object-based | File/object oriented |
                | Managed service | AWS manages infrastructure |
                | Pay-as-you-go | Usage-based pricing |
                
                ---
                
                # Important Concept — Durability
                
                ## Definition
                
                Probability your data survives without being lost.
                
                S3 durability:
                
                ```
                99.999999999%
                ```
                
                Meaning:
                
                ```
                Extremely unlikely to lose data
                ```
                
                AWS achieves this through:
                
                - replication
                - multiple servers
                - multiple Availability Zones
                
                ---
                
                # Important Concept — Availability
                
                ## Definition
                
                Probability service is accessible when requested.
                
                High availability means:
                
                ```
                S3 is accessible almost all the time
                ```
                
                ---
                
                # Important Concept — Scalability
                
                ## Definition
                
                Ability to grow without major redesign.
                
                S3 scalability means:
                
                ```
                Store billions of objects without manually managing disks/servers
                ```
                
                ---
                
                # Important Concept — Object Storage
                
                ## Definition
                
                Storage model where data is stored as objects instead of filesystem blocks.
                
                Each object contains:
                
                - data
                - metadata
                - key
                
                ---
                
                # S3 vs Traditional Filesystem
                
                | Traditional Filesystem | S3 |
                | --- | --- |
                | Folder hierarchy | Flat object namespace |
                | Attached disk | Distributed cloud storage |
                | Manual scaling | Automatic scaling |
                | Server-dependent | Independent service |
                | OS-managed | API-managed |
                
                ---
                
                # S3 vs EBS
                
                | S3 | EBS |
                | --- | --- |
                | Object storage | Block storage |
                | Massive scale | Attached to EC2 |
                | API access | Mounted disk |
                | Distributed | Single server storage |
                | Good for files | Good for OS/database disks |
                
                ---
                
                # Advantages of S3
                
                | Advantage | Explanation |
                | --- | --- |
                | Extremely scalable | Store huge amounts of data |
                | Highly durable | Very low data loss probability |
                | Managed infrastructure | No hardware management |
                | Flexible storage classes | Cost optimization |
                | Global access | Accessible worldwide |
                | Security features | IAM, bucket policies, encryption |
                | Integrates with AWS ecosystem | Lambda, CloudFront, Athena, etc. |
                
                ---
                
                # Disadvantages of S3
                
                | Disadvantage | Explanation |
                | --- | --- |
                | Not traditional filesystem | Cannot use like local disk directly |
                | Latency higher than local SSD | Network-based access |
                | Retrieval costs | Some classes charge for reads |
                | Eventual consistency for some configs | Certain bucket operations |
                | No multi-object transactions | No atomic updates across objects |
                
                ---
                
                # Important Mental Model
                
                S3 is NOT:
                
                ```
                A hard drive in the cloud
                ```
                
                S3 IS:
                
                ```
                A distributed object storage platform accessible through APIs
                ```
                
                ---
                
                # Real Production Architecture
                
                ```
                Users
                 ↓
                CloudFront CDN
                 ↓
                S3 bucket
                 ↓
                Images / videos / frontend assets
                ```
                
                OR
                
                ```
                Backend API
                 ↓
                S3
                 ↓
                Backups / uploads / documents
                ```
                
                ---
                
                # Why Companies Use S3
                
                Because:
                
                - infrastructure management is expensive
                - scaling storage manually is difficult
                - replication is hard
                - backups are complicated
                
                S3 abstracts all of that.
                
                ---
                
                # Interview-Level Understanding
                
                ## Why use S3 instead of storing files on EC2?
                
                Because:
                
                - EC2 disk is server-dependent
                - scaling becomes difficult
                - instance failure risks file loss
                - multiple servers cannot easily share local files
                
                S3 solves:
                
                - scalability
                - durability
                - shared access
                - global delivery
                
                ---

            - 2.Core Concepts
                - 2.2.1 Bucket
                    - Overall
                        
                        ## What is a Bucket?
                        
                        A bucket in Amazon Web Services [Amazon S3](https://aws.amazon.com/s3/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) is the top-level storage container used to store objects/files inside Amazon S3.
                        
                        Everything stored in S3 must exist inside a bucket.
                        
                        Simple structure:
                        
                        ```
                        Bucket
                         ├── Object
                         ├── Object
                         └── Object
                        ```
                        
                        Example:
                        
                        ```
                        my-images
                         ├── profile.png
                         ├── logo.jpg
                         └── banner.webp
                        ```
                        
                        Where:
                        
                        - `my-images` → bucket
                        - files inside → objects
                        
                        ---
                        
                    - What is a bucket
                        
                        A **Bucket** in Amazon Web Services [Amazon S3](https://aws.amazon.com/s3/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) is the top-level container used to store objects in Amazon S3.
                        
                        It is the fundamental organizational unit of S3.
                        
                        Everything stored in S3 must exist inside a bucket.
                        
                        ---
                        
                        # Simple Meaning
                        
                        Bucket is basically:
                        
                        ```
                        A cloud container that holds files/objects
                        ```
                        
                    - Why buckets exist
                        
                        AWS needs a way to:
                        
                        - organize data
                        - isolate customers
                        - apply permissions
                        - manage billing
                        - configure storage behavior
                        - control regions
                        - manage lifecycle policies
                        
                        Buckets solve this.
                        
                        # Why Buckets Exist
                        
                        Buckets exist because AWS needs a way to:
                        
                        - organize data
                        - isolate customer storage
                        - apply permissions
                        - manage billing
                        - configure regions
                        - apply lifecycle rules
                        - configure replication
                        - manage storage behavior
                        
                        Without buckets:
                        
                        ```
                        All S3 objects across AWS would exist in one massive uncontrolled storage space
                        ```
                        
                        Buckets create logical separation.
                        
                    - Global namespace
                        
                        ## What is Global Namespace?
                        
                        Bucket names in S3 are globally unique across AWS.
                        
                        Meaning:
                        
                        If somebody already created:
                        
                        ```
                        my-images
                        ```
                        
                        You cannot create another bucket with the same name anywhere in AWS.
                        
                        ---
                        
                        # Why AWS Uses Global Namespace
                        
                        Because bucket names become part of URLs.
                        
                        Example:
                        
                        ```
                        https://my-images.s3.amazonaws.com/logo.png
                        ```
                        
                        Global uniqueness guarantees:
                        
                        ```
                        URL uniqueness across AWS
                        ```
                        
                        ---
                        
                        # Important Understanding
                        
                        Bucket namespace is:
                        
                        ```
                        global
                        ```
                        
                        Object namespace is:
                        
                        ```
                        inside the bucket only
                        ```
                        
                        Meaning:
                        
                        - bucket names must be globally unique
                        - object names only need uniqueness inside their bucket
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ---
                        
                    - Bucket naming rules
                        
                        # Bucket Naming Rules
                        
                        ## Main Rules
                        
                        | Rule | Explanation |
                        | --- | --- |
                        | Must be globally unique | Across AWS |
                        | 3–63 characters | Length restriction |
                        | Lowercase only | No uppercase |
                        | Numbers allowed | Yes |
                        | Hyphens allowed | Yes |
                        | No spaces | Invalid |
                        | Cannot rename later | Permanent name |
                        
                        ---
                        
                        # Good Examples
                        
                        ```
                        unipos-assets
                        my-company-backups
                        frontend-prod-storage
                        ```
                        
                        ---
                        
                        # Bad Examples
                        
                        ```
                        MyBucket
                        test bucket
                        PROD_FILES
                        ```
                        
                        ---
                        
                        # Important Concept
                        
                        Bucket name becomes part of:
                        
                        - DNS
                        - URL
                        - API endpoints
                        
                        So AWS enforces strict naming standards.
                        
                        ---
                        
                    - Bucket region
                        
                        # Bucket Region
                        
                        ## What is Bucket Region?
                        
                        Bucket region is the AWS geographical location where bucket data is stored.
                        
                        Examples:
                        
                        - us-east-1
                        - eu-central-1
                        - ap-south-1
                        
                        ---
                        
                        # Why Region Exists
                        
                        Region affects:
                        
                        - latency
                        - legal compliance
                        - pricing
                        - replication
                        - disaster recovery
                        
                        ---
                        
                        # Example
                        
                        If users are near Uzbekistan:
                        
                        ```
                        Frankfurt
                        ```
                        
                        usually provides lower latency than:
                        
                        ```
                        Virginia
                        ```
                        
                        ---
                        
                        # Important Understanding
                        
                        After bucket creation:
                        
                        ```
                        Bucket region cannot be changed
                        ```
                        
                        To move regions:
                        
                        - create new bucket
                        - copy objects
                    - Bucket ownership
                        
                        ## What is Bucket Ownership?
                        
                        Every bucket belongs to one AWS account.
                        
                        Bucket owner controls:
                        
                        - permissions
                        - billing
                        - lifecycle rules
                        - replication
                        - bucket policies
                        - encryption settings
                        
                        ---
                        
                        # Important Understanding
                        
                        Even if:
                        
                        - another account uploads files
                        - public users upload objects
                        
                        bucket ownership still matters.
                        
                        ---
                        
                        # Why Ownership Exists
                        
                        Ownership provides:
                        
                        - security boundaries
                        - billing control
                        - administrative control
                        - access management
                    - Bucket types
                        
                        AWS supports multiple bucket types.
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ## General Purpose Buckets
                        
                        Default bucket type.
                        
                        Used for:
                        
                        - applications
                        - uploads
                        - backups
                        - websites
                        - media storage
                        
                        Most S3 workloads use this type.
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ## Directory Buckets
                        
                        Optimized for:
                        
                        - low latency
                        - hierarchical directories
                        - S3 Express One Zone
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ## Table Buckets
                        
                        Optimized for:
                        
                        - analytics
                        - tabular datasets
                        - Apache Iceberg
                        
                        Used with:
                        
                        - Athena
                        - Redshift
                        - Spark
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ## Vector Buckets
                        
                        Optimized for:
                        
                        - vector embeddings
                        - AI similarity search
                        - machine learning systems
                    - Bucket-level configurations
                        
                        # Bucket-Level Configurations
                        
                        Buckets can configure many behaviors.
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ## Common Configurations
                        
                        | Feature | Purpose |
                        | --- | --- |
                        | Versioning | Keep object history |
                        | Lifecycle Rules | Auto-delete/archive |
                        | Encryption | Protect data |
                        | Replication | Copy objects |
                        | Bucket Policy | Access control |
                        | Logging | Audit requests |
                        | CORS | Browser access rules |
                        | Public Access Block | Prevent exposure |
                        
                        ---
                        
                        # Important Understanding
                        
                        Configurations are often:
                        
                        ```
                        bucket-wide
                        ```
                        
                        not per object.
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ---
                        
                    - Real production usage
                        
                        # Real Production Usage
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ## Static Website Hosting
                        
                        ```
                        CloudFront
                         ↓
                        S3 Bucket
                         ↓
                        React frontend
                        ```
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ## Backup Storage
                        
                        ```
                        PostgreSQL backups
                         ↓
                        ZIP files
                         ↓
                        S3 Bucket
                        ```
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ## User Uploads
                        
                        ```
                        Frontend
                         ↓
                        Presigned URL
                         ↓
                        S3 Bucket
                        ```
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ## Media Storage
                        
                        ```
                        Videos
                        Images
                        Documents

                        ```
                        
                        stored inside buckets.
                        
                    - Pros and cons
                        
                        # Pros and Cons
                        
                        ## Pros
                        
                        | Advantage | Explanation |
                        | --- | --- |
                        | Massive scalability | Billions of objects |
                        | Strong durability | Multi-AZ storage |
                        | Flexible configurations | Policies/lifecycle/encryption |
                        | Global accessibility | Internet-accessible APIs |
                        | Managed infrastructure | No disk management |
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ## Cons
                        
                        |  | Explanation |
                        | --- | --- |
                        | Global naming conflicts | Names may already exist |
                        | Cannot rename | Permanent bucket names |
                        | Region immutable | Hard to relocate |
                        | Misconfiguration risk | Public exposure possible |
                    - Interview understanding
                        
                        # Common Interview Question
                        
                        ## Why are bucket names globally unique?
                        
                        Because:
                        
                        ```
                        bucket names are part of global DNS/URLs
                        ```
                        
                        ---
                        
                        # Common Interview Question
                        
                        ## Why not store files on EC2 instead?
                        
                        Because buckets provide:
                        
                        - higher durability
                        - scalability
                        - easier sharing
                        - lifecycle management
                        - global access
                        - managed storage
                        
                        ---
                        
                        # Important Mental Model
                        
                        Bucket is NOT:
                        
                        ```
                        just a folder
                        ```
                        
                        Bucket IS:
                        
                        ```
                        a globally unique distributed storage container with configurable security, lifecycle, replication, and storage behavior
                        ```
                        
                - 2.2.2 Objects
                    - Overall
                        
                        # Overall
                        
                        ## What is an Object?
                        
                        An object in Amazon Web Services [Amazon S3](https://aws.amazon.com/s3/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) is the fundamental unit of data stored inside a bucket.
                        
                        In simple terms:
                        
                        ```
                        Object = File + Metadata + Unique Identifier
                        ```
                        
                        Everything stored in S3 becomes an object.
                        
                        Examples:
                        
                        - image.png
                        - backup.zip
                        - video.mp4
                        - invoice.pdf
                        - dataset.csv
                        
                        ---
                        
                        # What is an Object
                        
                        An object contains:
                        
                        - actual file data
                        - metadata about the file
                        - unique key/name
                        
                        ---
                        
                        # Simple Example
                        
                        ```
                        Bucket:
                        my-images
                        
                        Object:
                        profile.png
                        ```
                        
                        Internally:
                        
                        ```
                        Object
                         ├── Data
                         ├── Metadata
                         └── Key
                        ```
